content.overview: A section 138 notice is the written demand required by proviso (b) to section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881. The payee or holder in due course must demand the cheque amount in writing within thirty days of receiving information from the bank that the cheque was returned unpaid. The drawer then has fifteen days from receipt of the notice to pay. The notice is a condition of the offence. It is not the complaint. The complaint is filed under section 142 after the fifteen days expire unpaid, within one month of that cause of action unless delay is condoned.
content.short: A Statutory Legal Demand Notice under Section 138 proviso (b) of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 is an indispensable condition precedent to filing a criminal complaint for cheque dishonour. It must demand the exact cheque amount within 30 days of receiving the return memo, affording a mandatory 15-day cure window to the drawer.
content.detailed:
Core Drafting Skeleton & Statutory Roadmaps for Section 138 NI Act Notice

1. Heading, Reference & Dispatch Medium
   • ADVOCATE CHAMBERS / LETTERHEAD
   • Date of Notice: [Must be within 30 days of receipt of bank memo: s. 138 proviso (b)]
   • Mode of Dispatch: Registered Post with Acknowledgment Due (RPAD) / Speed Post / Email.

2. Addressee Particulars
   • To: [Name of Drawer / Account Holder]
   • If a Corporate Entity: To M/s [Company Name] through its Managing Director / Directors, with specific averments under Section 141 NI Act.

3. Authority Clause
   • "Under instructions from and on behalf of my client, [Name of Payee/Complainant], resident of …, I hereby serve upon you this Statutory Legal Demand Notice under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881."

4. Transactional Relationship & Legally Enforceable Debt
   • Precise details of goods delivered, services rendered, or loan disbursed.
   • Clear recital that the cheque was issued towards discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability (supported by the statutory presumption under Section 139 NI Act).

5. Cheque Particulars & Presentation Details
   • Cheque Number, Cheque Date, Drawn on [Bank & Branch], for a sum of Rs. [X]/- (Rupees … in words).
   • Date of presentation of cheque within its 3-month statutory validity.
   • Bank Return Memo details: Date of memo, reason for dishonour (e.g., "Funds Insufficient", "Account Closed", "Stop Payment").

6. Vicarious Liability under Section 141 (If Accused is a Company/Firm)
   • Mandatory averment as mandated in SMS Pharmaceuticals: "That Noticee Nos. 2 and 3 were at the time of commission of the offence in charge of, and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business, and the cheque was issued with their consent and connivance."

7. The Mandatory 15-Day Demand Requisition
   • Strict demand for the exact cheque amount: "I hereby call upon you to pay the aforesaid cheque amount of Rs. [X]/- within 15 (fifteen) days from the date of receipt of this notice."
   • Clear warning of penal consequences: Failure to pay within 15 days will result in the filing of a criminal complaint under Section 138 read with Section 142 NI Act, rendering the accused liable to imprisonment up to 2 years and/or fine up to twice the cheque amount, alongside interim compensation under Section 143A.

8. Advocate Signature & Endorsement

Statutory Limitation & Chronology Chain:
• Day 0: Payee receives dishonour memo from the bank.
• Day 1 to 30: Payee must dispatch statutory notice under s. 138 proviso (b).
• Notice Served: Drawer gets 15 days from receipt to make payment (s. 138 proviso (c)).
• Day 16: Cause of action arises if payment is not made (premature complaint before Day 16 is invalid: Yogendra Pratap Singh).
• Next 30 Days: Payee must file criminal complaint before the jurisdictional Magistrate under Section 142(1)(b).
• Territorial Jurisdiction (s. 142(2) NI Act 2015): Court having jurisdiction over the branch where the payee maintains their bank account.

cases.name: C.C. Alavi Haji v. Palapetty Muhammed
cases.holding: Deemed service of notice under Section 27 General Clauses Act applies when notice is correctly addressed and sent by registered post. A drawer claiming non-receipt must pay within 15 days of court summons to avert prosecution.
cases.relevance: Presumption of service of statutory notice and protection against evasive drawers.

cases.name: S.M.S. Pharmaceuticals Ltd. v. Neeta Bhalla
cases.holding: Specific averment in notice and complaint that the director was in charge of and responsible to the company for the conduct of its business is a sine qua non for vicarious liability under Section 141.
cases.relevance: Mandatory pleading requirements for prosecuting company directors in cheque bounce.

cases.name: Dashrath Rupsingh Rathod v. State of Maharashtra
cases.holding: Led to the Negotiable Instruments (Amendment) Act, 2015 inserting Section 142(2), which codified that jurisdiction lies where the payee delivers the cheque for collection through their bank account.
cases.relevance: Territorial jurisdiction benchmark for filing Section 138 complaints.

bareActPointers: Section 138 NI Act (Dishonour of cheque for insufficiency of funds)
Section 139 NI Act (Presumption in favour of holder)
Section 141 NI Act (Offences by companies and director liability)
Section 142(1)(b) & 142(2) NI Act (Limitation and territorial jurisdiction)
Section 143A NI Act (Power to direct interim compensation up to 20%)
examTips: Notice must demand the exact cheque amount; demanding compound interest or arbitrary damages without segregating the principal cheque amount can invalidate the notice (Suman Sethi).
A complaint filed before the expiry of 15 days from notice delivery is premature and liable to be quashed (Yogendra Pratap Singh v. Savitri Pandey).
Under Section 142(2)(a) NI Act, jurisdiction is determined by the bank branch where the payee maintains their account, not the drawer bank.
Under Section 143A NI Act, the Magistrate can order interim compensation up to 20% of the cheque amount during summary trial.

enhancement.definition: A section 138 legal notice is the written demand for the cheque amount, issued by the payee or holder in due course within thirty days of receiving bank information of dishonour.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Without this demand, and without failure to pay within fifteen days of its receipt, the section 138 offence does not mature. The notice does not itself seize the court.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, section 138 provisos (b) and (c), and section 142. The NI subject topics on those sections are the offence and cognizance notes; this topic is the notice format.
essentialIngredients: Cheque number, date, amount and drawer
Bank return and date the payee received that information
Demand for the cheque amount in writing
Issued within thirty days of that information
Addressee is the drawer, at a traceable address
Proof of dispatch and later service preserved
No complaint prayer inside the notice
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The notice identifies the parties, the debt or liability for which the cheque was issued, the cheque details, presentation, and the return reason as communicated by the bank. The operative paragraph demands payment of the cheque amount within fifteen days of receipt. It should be dated and sent so that the thirty-day proviso can be proved: the date the payee received the return information must appear. A demand for compensation or costs does not replace the demand for the cheque amount. Service is a later proof point; the format should keep the address, mode of sending, and postal or courier receipt. After fifteen days from receipt without payment, the cause of action for the complaint arises. This format does not compute jurisdiction. That is section 142(2).
examples: Return memo received on 1 June. Notice dated 20 June demanding the cheque amount is inside proviso (b).
Notice sent on day 40 after the memo was received. Proviso (b) is missed.
Notice gives fifteen days to pay. A complaint filed on day 5 after receipt is premature.
enhancement.problemApplication: Fix the date bank information was received, count thirty days, check that the cheque amount is demanded, and wait fifteen days after receipt before treating the offence as complete.
distinctions: Thirty-day issue period vs fifteen-day cure
Demand for the cheque amount vs a general lawyer's letter
Notice format vs territorial jurisdiction under section 142(2)

keyTakeaways: The notice must demand the cheque amount.
It must go within thirty days of receiving bank information.
The drawer has fifteen days from receipt to pay.
The notice is not the complaint.
A late demand does not mature the offence.

content.study: Demand the cheque amount, identify the cheque and the return, and send it within thirty days of receiving the bank's information. Do not treat a reminder after the thirty days as compliance. Do not file the complaint inside the fifteen-day cure window.
